name: Spike
about: Research or experiment to resolve uncertainty and guide subsequent work.
type: Spike

<!-- Guidance for the author. Delete these comments before submitting; they stay in
the text even though the page hides them.
- Keep every section except Starting evidence, which you can delete, heading
  included, if it would add nothing.
- Make the issue understandable on its own. Say each thing once; if it fits several
  sections, choose one.
- Define the uncertainty to resolve, not a solution that must be proved right.
- Separate confirmed facts from hypotheses. Do not invent missing details.
- Use the names found in the code or product, and summarize any source the reader
  cannot open. -->

## Context and decision to inform
<!-- The current situation and the decision or work this spike's findings will
inform. Name the parent epic and any issues waiting on it. -->

## Questions
<!-- The specific questions to answer, marking which are essential. -->

## Starting evidence
<!-- Observations, previous attempts, code or research, and what each
establishes. -->

## Scope and limit
<!-- What is in and out of scope, and a limit that can be checked, such as a time
box, a number of approaches or a cost ceiling. Say what happens at the limit. -->

## Expected output
<!-- What will answer the questions, including the supporting evidence and
remaining uncertainty it should show, and where it will be recorded. Say whether an
inconclusive result is acceptable and whether any code is expected to be
merged. -->
